title: The ladder and the rope, in order
caption: the argument in reading order

nodes.text: A skill is a ladder: ordered rungs, climbed in advance-set order.
A skill is a rope: many weak crossing strands, none running the whole length.
Ladder-trained skill collapses when the problem turns sideways.
Splicing, not climbing — short strands joined until the join disappears.
The objection: ropes cannot be inspected.
The objection lands: a braid hides its gaps until it is loaded.
Keep both pictures: climb mapped ground, braid unmapped, and know which you are on.
